# Policy, verdict vocabulary and fingerprint scheme: scripts/sast-register.sh
# verdict: real | false-positive | deliberate | blocked | unreviewed
# 'line' is navigation only and is refreshed each run; it is NOT part of

# to unreviewed, because the code the verdict described has changed.

Logged value is the description bus.ResolveTokenSource returns: fixed text plus, at most, the RASPUTIN_CP_JOIN_TOKEN_FILE path from the agent's own environment (node.env / the unit) or the constant proto.BusAgentTokenPath. Never the token, nothing from a bus message or request, and formatted with %q so a hand-edited value cannot forge a log line. gosec does not treat %q as a sanitizer. Same site and same reasoning as the row this replaces (59eab2c2970166d8): ResolveTokenSource now also returns the proto.TokenSource* value the agent reports, which changed the snippet and so the fingerprint. The third return value is one of three package constants and is not logged here. Trip-wire: void if this line ever logs the token itself or a value taken from a bus message.
Logged value is internal, not user-influenced: the NOTIFY_SOCKET path from our own environment and injected-fault names from the test hook.

atrest.syncDir opens the directory of a file the helper just wrote, to fsync the rename, and only syncs and closes the handle. The directory is filepath.Dir of the caller's own path: the agent's state tree (RASPUTIN_AGENT_STATE_DIR plus a subsystem's fixed subdirectory, and for an app the id docker.safeAppID has already refused unless it is a single path element), the systemd-resolved drop-in directory, or the dnsmasq hostsdir. No component is request input.

Checked against the Go source, not assumed: crypto/tls documents "on clients, session ticket support is also disabled if ClientSessionCache is nil". Neither BMC client sets one and net/http injects none, so resumption never happens and VerifyPeerCertificate runs on every handshake. NOTE: adding a ClientSessionCache to either client silently weakens the cert pin and must re-open this row.

TOFU fingerprint capture. Verification is deliberately off because the board mints a self-signed cert at the epoch that is permanently expired, so no chain check can pass; the operator confirms the displayed digest. The VerifyPeerCertificate hook here only records, it does not judge.

math/rand/v2 jitters a reconnect delay so nodes that lost the controlplane together do not re-dial in lockstep. Nothing security-relevant depends on the value: it is never a key, token, nonce, id or session material, and an attacker who could predict every node's jitter gains only the timing of a dial that is retried forever anyway. The only property needed is spread, which any PRNG gives; crypto/rand would add an error path to a timer for no gain.

Certificate pinning, which is STRICTER than the chain check it skips (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#448). A chain check accepts any certificate a trusted issuer signed; the VerifyConnection callback on the next lines accepts exactly one public key, by the SHA-256 of its SubjectPublicKeyInfo, and returns an error for anything else. VerifyConnection (not VerifyPeerCertificate) runs on every handshake, resumed ones included, so a session cache cannot bypass it. The chain check cannot be used here by design: the bus certificate is self-signed and its dates are deliberately ignored, because a Pi boots before NTP. TRIP-WIRE: this verdict is void if the VerifyConnection assignment is removed, made conditional, or stops comparing the full digest; the fingerprint covers only this line and will not notice. Tested: agent/internal/bus/pin_test.go TestClient_PinnedTLS (wrong pin refused) and api/internal/bustls/functional_test.go TestFunctional_OfferMode.

Opens the directory of the pin file to fsync it after the rename. The path is filepath.Dir of PinFilePath(stateDir) = <RASPUTIN_AGENT_STATE_DIR>/bus/pin, derived by the agent from its own environment. Nothing on this path comes from a request or a bus message; the bus.pin command carries only the pin value, which is validated and never used as a path.

Reads the controlplane agent's join token file. Reading an operator-chosen path is the point of the setting, and the agent already runs as root.

argv-form exec.CommandContext with no shell; the binary is the literal "docker". Every argument is built by the builders in this file: compose project names (projectName(appID), a lower-cased ULID), the tile's volume name as the VALUE of a `--filter label=k=v` argument (never a free operand, so a leading `-` cannot read as an option), container ids and mount destinations parsed back out of docker's own `ps`/`inspect` output, and container-side paths path.Join'd onto that absolute destination (so `sqlite3 <src>` is never option-shaped). The one place a value enters CODE is sqlite3VacuumArgv's SQL literal, where `'` is doubled; python3BackupArgv passes both paths in argv and its program text is a constant. The inspect template is a constant — the volume name is matched in Go afterwards, not interpolated. TRIP-WIRE: a builder that interpolates a name into a template or a `sh -c` string reopens this.

argv-form exec.CommandContext of the literal "docker" binary, no shell. It is the one docker exec in the package: ComposeBackend.run (compose up/down/ps/config) and the volume verbs in volumes.go and appvolumes.go all come through dockerFor to here. Compose vectors are composeArgs(composePath, projectName(appID), constant verb args): composePath is filepath.Join of the agent's state root with an app id that Deploy, Stop and Pull refuse unless it is one path element (safeAppID), and the project name is the value of `-p`. Volume vectors are built by the *Args builders from constants plus docker volume names, and every name reaching those builders has passed proto.ParseAppVolumeName (rasp_<26-char Crockford ULID>_<volume>) or proto.IsAnonymousVolumeName (exactly 64 lower-case hex), refused otherwise, so a name cannot begin with `-`. Names appear either as the VALUE of a `--filter volume=<name>` / `--filter label=<k>=<project>` argument or as free operands placed after a literal `--` (volumeInspectJSONArgs, volumeRmArgs, containerInspectArgs, whose container ids are docker's own `ps --quiet --no-trunc` output), so option parsing has already ended when they are read. Removal goes only through gateAndRemove, which refuses a volume whose docker labels disagree with how it was identified (compose project label for a named volume; com.docker.volume.anonymous and no project label for an anonymous one) or that any container references; the reaper path additionally applies the api ledger to the owner (named: parsed from the name; anonymous: from exactly one per-app record). TRIP-WIRE: a builder that drops the `--`, takes a name that skipped both shape checks, or moves to `sh -c` reopens this.

Path is filepath.Join of the agent's own restore-record directory (RestoreRecordDir(stateDir), set from RASPUTIN_STATE_DIR in main.go) with an entry name this process just listed from that directory with os.ReadDir. No component derives from the bus, a request or a volume: the records are written only by writeRestoreRecord in this file, under this agent's state dir, mode 0600. What the record NAMES (a staging path) is then trusted only by shape — its base name must carry the restore-staging prefix — and the only action on it is RemoveAll of a directory this agent created beside a volume. Covered by TestSweepRestoreStagingRemovesOnlyRecordedStagingTrees, which asserts a record naming a non-staging path is left alone along with what it names.

Every path here is composed by this package, never taken from a bus field. The volume root comes from the runtime (docker volume inspect's Mountpoint, or the mock's own directory), and every file opened under it is a path filepath.WalkDir returned from walking that root — the api sends a volume NAME (BackupStageVolumeCmd.Volume) and never a path. The staged file is filepath.Join(stagingRoot, cmd.StagingName) where StagingName has passed proto.BackupValidStagingName — the SAME predicate the write verb applies: letters, digits, - _ . only, no separator, no leading dot, no ./.. — with a `.partial-` prefix, and stagingRoot is agent-side config (storage.StagingRoot). A sqlite snapshot substitute is filepath.Join(volRoot, .rasputin-quiesce, dbRel) with dbRel a walk result. TRIP-WIRE: a verb that takes a path instead of a name, or a relaxed BackupValidStagingName, makes this row real — the shape check IS the control.

The transfer verb opens the staged tar it is about to seal: filepath.Join(s.stagingRoot, cmd.StagingName), where StagingName has passed proto.BackupValidStagingName in validateTransfer (letters, digits, - _ . only, at most 128 chars, no separator, no leading dot, no `.`/`..`) and stagingRoot is this agent's own configured root (storage.StagingRoot). Same containment as the write verb's rows above: the join cannot leave the root, and it is Lstat'd and required to be a regular file before the open. The destination URI and the credential in the same command never touch the filesystem. TRIP-WIRE: a path field on BackupTransferCmd, or a StagingName that skips the shape check, reopens this.

Marker paths are filepath.Join(markerDir, name) where markerDir is agent config (<stateDir>/quiesce-armed) and name is either a file os.ReadDir returned from that directory (SweepArmedStops) or markerName(appID), which maps every rune outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] to `_` before appending .json — so a bus-supplied app id cannot carry a separator or traverse. The bytes read back are json.Unmarshal'd into armedStop (ids and a timestamp) and used only to choose WHICH app to `compose start`; a marker that does not decode is logged and left alone. TRIP-WIRE: reading any other field out of a marker, or building the name from anything but markerName, reopens this.

The one exec seam for the whole blockdev backend. There is no shell: exec.CommandContext takes an argv slice. `name` is never caller-supplied — it comes from the tools map, populated only by exec.LookPath over the fixed requiredTools/optionalTools lists, and tool() falls back to the same literal names. Every operand that originates off-box is regex-validated first (checkDevicePath / checkPartUUID reject anything not matching ^/dev/... or a UUID, which also stops a value being read as an option), and lsblk gets an explicit `--` separator before its operand. The indirection is load-bearing rather than incidental: it is what lets blockdev_test.go assert that a REFUSED claim never reached wipefs/sfdisk/mkfs, which cannot be tested on hardware. Inlining exec.CommandContext at each of the eight call sites would produce eight copies of this same finding and delete that test.

Both components of the joined path are ours. mountPath is filepath.Join(mountRoots[purpose], partUUID): the roots come from proto's purpose spec table (compile-time constants) and partUUID has passed checkPartUUID. name is the marker filename from that same spec table, also a constant — readMarkerFile has no caller that passes anything else. Nothing on this path derives from a request, a bus message, or the disk's own contents. What IS untrusted here is the file's CONTENT, not its path: enumeration reads markers off disks nobody has confirmed anything about. That is handled at this call site by io.LimitReader(f, markerMaxBytes+1) — deliberately not by measuring after os.ReadFile, which would read a hostile multi-gigabyte marker into memory on a Pi 4 before rejecting it. Re-open this row if readMarkerFile ever gains a caller whose name or mountPath is not a constant and a validated PARTUUID.

The directory fsync that makes the marker rename durable. mountPath here is the return of mountPartition — filepath.Join(mountRoot, partUUID) with partUUID already matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$, so it cannot contain a separator or traverse out of mountRoot. The handle is opened only to call Sync() and is closed immediately; no content is read from it.

The probe path is composed entirely by this package: filepath.Join(mountPath, proto.StorageHealthProbeDir, "probe-"+hex(8 random bytes)). mountPath is what Backend.Inspect resolved for a checkPartUUID'd partition UUID (the same root archive.go's rows rest on), the directory is a constant, and the file name is minted from crypto/rand in this function — no request, bus field or operator input contributes a byte of it, and the handler only passes the ack's own MountPath in. Opened with O_CREATE|O_EXCL so an existing entry (a symlink planted on the disk) is refused rather than followed. TRIP-WIRE: taking a path or a name from StorageInspectCmd makes this row real.

Nothing secret passes through it. The agent's own copy of the same CA is written by atrest.WritePublicFile (trust.go, installMeshCA).

0644 is correct for a detached CMS signature: these exact bytes are published as a public asset on the GitHub release and served unauthenticated by the api at /api/bundles/{sha}/sig, so there is nothing to keep confidential. It sits in the agent's bundle cache, which is 0700 (atrest.EnsureSecretDir), so the file's own mode grants nobody anything either way. The verification's soundness does not rest on this file's permissions — a tampered .sig fails the chain check, and an attacker already holding root on the node replaces the agent rather than the signature (the same reasoning the threat model applies to the baked trust anchor, A2).

os.Chmod(dir, 0o700) on the Grafana socket DIRECTORY (geekdojo-brain#453). G302's 0600 ceiling is a file rule: a directory without the owner's execute bit cannot be entered, so Grafana could not bind its socket in it. 0700 is the tightest usable mode and is the control itself: owner-only, no group or other bits. The socket inside is 0600 (socket_mode), and both are asserted by the functional test against real Grafana. Same shape as the agent's /run/rasputin-caddy directory (#329).

Both components of every staged path are checked at the join, in stagedPath. THE DIRECTORY is the target node's staging root, which arrives in BackupPreflightAck.StagingRoot rather than being derived here — the api derived its own until 2026-09-02 and got a different answer from the agent on every shipping image. Two controls bound it: step 1 (runValidate) refuses any target whose NodeID is not RunConfig.SelfNodeID, so the ack can only have come from the agent on THIS host, a process already running as root beside the api and with nothing to gain by steering it; and checkStagingRoot then requires an absolute path equal to filepath.Clean of itself, applied both on the way in from the ack and on the way back out of the job ledger, so a relative path, a `..`, a doubled separator or a trailing slash never reaches os.MkdirAll, CleanStaging or a file open. THE NAME is minted by this package as stagingName(generationID, kind), where the id comes from proto.BackupGenerationID (a UTC timestamp, the ULID job id's tail with every non-alphanumeric mapped out, and a scope constant), and is re-checked with proto.BackupValidStagingName — the SAME predicate the agent's write verb applies to what it is sent: one path component of [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 128 chars, no separator, no leading dot. So the join is always a direct child of the staging root. Nothing is caller-supplied: storage.RunSpec has no path field, and POST /api/backup/runs decodes with DisallowUnknownFields so an invented one is a 400 rather than a value. TRIP-WIRE: dropping the SelfNodeID check in runValidate, or building a staged path by any route other than stagedPath, makes these rows real — those two checks ARE the control.

artifactsig is a library and sigPath is its parameter, so this was derived from the call sites rather than from the line. catalogsync passes MkdirTemp dir + the package constant assetSig, or filepath.Join(s.dir, fmt.Sprintf(bundleName, version))+".sig" where version is an int from strconv.Atoi — no separator can enter either. The agent updater passes <artifact>.sig where the artifact is stateDir/bundles/<BundleID>.rootfs and BundleID is spec.BundleSHA256, hex with no separators. The agent no longer relies on the api's good behaviour for that last point: UpdateInstallCmd.LocalPath and BundleID used to reach this line unvalidated, and every backend now resolves them through agent/internal/updater/bundlepath.go, which requires the id to be one safe filename component and a non-empty LocalPath to land inside the bundle store. gosec sees `nonce := make([]byte, NonceSize)` — a zero slice — reaching a Seal call, and cannot follow the per-chunk mutation inside sealChunk, which writes the big-endian chunk counter into nonce[0:8] and the last-chunk flag into nonce[8] before every call. So the nonce is a counter, not a constant. The (key, nonce) pair is unique twice over: the content key is derived fresh for EVERY call to Seal (a new ephemeral X25519 keypair per run, hashed into the HKDF salt alongside the recipient's public key), and within one run the counter increments per chunk. This is the age/STREAM construction. Moved from api/internal/storage/seal.go unchanged (2026-09-03) so the agent seals volumes with the same code; NewSealedStream calls Seal once per member, so a member never shares a content key with anything. TRIP-WIRE: this row becomes real the moment a content key is reused across two calls to Seal — i.e. if the ephemeral keypair is ever hoisted out of the function or cached per target.
